snippet.title: THIS is The Pressure Relief Valve For Taking Back Your Metal and Emotional Health ft. Jenny Locklin
snippet.description:
Joe's Free Book: https://joesfreebook.com/

If you’d like to join world-renowned Entrepreneurs at the next Genius Network® Event – then apply today for your invitation to attend at https://geniusnetwork.com/event/.

You track your sleep, optimize your diet, and refine your business strategy—but are you neglecting the one free tool that can save your mental and emotional health?

In this lighthearted yet profound talk, Jenny Locklin (the "Undercover Speaker" and daughter of Hall of Fame speaker Joel Weldon) reveals why a sense of humor is the ultimate "pressure relief valve." When the stress of entrepreneurship builds up, humor prevents system failure.

Jenny shares hilarious and touching personal stories—from her family's terrible matching outfits to navigating her mother's dementia with Snapchat filters, and even getting roasted by her iPhone's Face ID after skin cancer surgery. Learn actionable ways to find "slivers of humor" in your darkest moments, accept what you can't change, and use the "Mistake Break" to build resilience and connection with your team.

Key Takeaways:
• The Hidden Benefits of Humor: How laughing strengthens your immune system, acts as an antidepressant, and keeps you looking young.
• The "Pressure Relief Valve" Concept: Why humor is essential for preventing emotional and mental burnout.
• Finding Humor in the Past: How looking at old photos (and questionable fashion choices) can instantly shift your perspective.
• Accepting the Unchangeable: Jenny’s hilarious take on accepting her height and the awkwardness of hugging tall friends.
• The "Mistake Break": A simple leadership exercise to build psychological safety and grace within your team.
• Finding Light in the Dark: A touching story of how Snapchat filters created moments of joy during a parent's battle with dementia.
• Self-Deprecation as a Superpower: How a failed Face ID login after surgery provided a much-needed laugh.

What does it take to truly change the world, scale your impact, and maintain your own happiness in the process? In this powerhouse compilation from the Genius Network stage, some of the world's most brilliant minds—including Tony Robbins, Peter Diamandis, Naveen Jain, Kathy Kolbe, Alex Epstein, Simon Bowen, and Joe Polish—share their most profound insights on business, psychology, and the future of humanity.

This multi-speaker masterclass covers everything from redefining the "impossible" and completely transforming the global education system, to the neuroscience of ethical selling and why "work-life balance" is a complete illusion.

• Kathy Kolbe on Instinct: How to tap into your "conation" (your natural instinct for action) to thrive and innovate during periods of massive global disruption.
• Alex Epstein on the "F-Word": Why Freedom is the ultimate, unapologetic root cause of human flourishing and why entrepreneurs must fight for it.
• Naveen Jain on Solving Billion-Dollar Problems: Why fixing the broken, industrial-era education system requires a shift to "fixed learning, variable time."
• Simon Bowen on The Sage Model: Why selling is the ultimate force for good when done ethically, and why you must stop playing the "Hero" and become the "Sage" (like Yoda) for your clients.
• Joe Polish on Connection vs. Conning: Why transforming other people's "bad news" into "good news" is the core of entrepreneurship, and why your private victories must always precede your public ones.

snippet.title: The Truth Is in Your Numbers: How Accurate Records Drive Your Success ft. Joel Weldon
snippet.description:
Joe's Free Book: https://joesfreebook.com

"Without numerical data, you're just another person with an opinion." In this inspiring talk, Hall of Fame speaker Joel Weldon (age 84!) proves why tracking your numbers is the ultimate key to success, health, and happiness.

Joel reveals his personal records from over 50 years—from tracking his weight every single morning since 1991 (maintaining a 186.5lb average) to logging 2,000 days of joy on his houseboat. He explains how measuring what matters—whether it's business metrics, physical health, or moments of pure joy—allows you to improve, control, and treasure your life.

You'll see his actual logbooks, hear about his birthday ritual of skiing his age (yes, even at 84!), and discover why starting a simple "Numbers Journal" today could change your future. Plus, don't miss the hilarious "F-Bomb Log" he kept for Joe Polish!

Key Takeaways:
* The Truth Is in Your Numbers: How Accurate Records Reveal Patterns and Drive Your Success
* Why numbers never lie, and how they quietly predict your future success.
* The story of a 17-year-old caddie who discovered that tracking his tips could change his entire life.
* How one Hall-of-Fame speaker used feedback cards and weight logs to stay consistent for 50+ years.
* The shocking truth about what people think they do vs. what their numbers prove, and how to close that gap.
* Why joy deserves data too, and how tracking what makes you happiest can help you live longer and happier
* What happens when you start measuring birthdays, workouts, and even F-bombs... and why it’s never too late to start your own numbers journal.

Timestamps:

01:30 – Joel’s first logbook at age 17 (Caddying income)
02:45 – Business Numbers: Tracking speaking feedback for 50 years
03:45 – Body Numbers: 12,000+ daily weigh-in entries since 1991

snippet.title: How to Help Your Loved Ones battle ADDICTION: 8 Tips from the Experts Feat. Dr. Gabor Maté
snippet.description:
Joe's Free Book: https://joesfreebook.com/

What do you do when someone you love lies, steals, and spirals in active addiction? How can families hold onto compassion while setting boundaries with a child, spouse, or friend lost in the grip of substance abuse? In this deeply moving and insightful conversation, we explore the hard truths of addiction—and the powerful healing that’s possible when we shift our perspective from judgment to understanding.

You’ll hear real stories of addiction, denial, and breakthrough moments. We unpack the most critical questions:

- What's the difference between addiction and dependence?
- Why do so many addicts promise to stop—and then use again?
- How can families stop trying to “fix” someone and start healing themselves?
- What are the two rational responses a loved one can take when dealing with an addict?

Featuring hard-won wisdom and raw honesty, this episode is for anyone feeling heartbroken, confused, or stuck in the chaos that addiction brings. Whether you're the one struggling or you love someone who is, this video is a compassionate guide to understanding the deep pain behind the behavior—and what true help and healing can look like.

snippet.title: 90% of Business Success Comes From THIS One Thing (Must See) Ft. Dan Sullivan & Brian Tracy
snippet.description:
Joe's Free Book: https://joesfreebook.com/

If you’d like to join world-renowned Entrepreneurs at the next Genius Network® Event – then apply today for your invitation to attend at https://geniusnetwork.com/event/.

In this wide-ranging presentation at Genius Network, the discussion dives deep into the core mechanics of successful entrepreneurship, the biological reality of decision-making, and the urgent necessity of defending free speech and cognitive liberty in a highly polarized culture.

The first half explores hard-hitting business strategy: why traditional university entrepreneurship programs often fail, how to distinguish between a symptom and a root problem, and the operational power of practicing Strategic Thinking Time. The second half shifts into a candid conversation on cultural warfare, the financial realities of standing up for traditional values, and the heavy personal sacrifices required to protect individual freedom and institutional checks and balances.

Key Takeaways:
• The Fallacy of the Business Plan: Data shows that 49 out of 50 successful businesses are started without a formal business plan, challenging the foundational teachings of mainstream academic institutions.
• The Power of Focus: In a fast-moving world, simultaneous focus remains the absolute baseline for scaling a company and doubling both net revenue and personal time off.
• Fast vs. Slow Thinking: Neuroscientific models show that entrepreneurs routinely sabotage long-term financial outcomes by using reactionary "fast thinking" on complex decisions that explicitly require analytical "slow thinking."
• Zero-Based Thinking (ZBT): A critical mental framework requiring leaders to ruthlessly evaluate every relationship, employee, and product line by asking: "Knowing what I now know, would I start this up again today?"
• The Law of Constraints: Identifying the singular Choke Point or limiting factor in a business that establishes the literal speed at which financial goals are realized.
• The Freedom Cycle vs. Captivity Cycle: Understanding how innovative thinkers operate out of intrinsic "wanting" to build momentum, while legacy environments trap individuals in external "needing" and constant justification.
• The Cost of Free Speech: A raw assessment of the real-world repercussions—including systemic boycotts, canceled contracts, and direct security threats—that occur when public figures refuse to comply with cultural echo chambers.

Part I: The Mechanics of Clear Thinking & Scaling Profitability

"If people are afraid to say things, not just in your company but in the culture, you stop creating the friction required to get to good ideas. We have to be willing to talk about the elephant in the room."
45:00 — Repercussions of truth-telling: Navigating death threats and security frameworks

snippet.description:

Joe Polish sits down with renowned physician and author Dr. Gabor Maté to explore the true roots of human addiction, trauma, and suffering. They dismantle the stigma surrounding substance abuse, revealing how all addictions—from drugs and alcohol to "respectable" addictions like workaholism and power—stem from a desperate human need for connection and an attempt to numb deep-seated pain.

You'll discover why the prison system entrenches addiction, the critical difference between overt and developmental trauma, and why letting go can sometimes be more powerful than forced forgiveness.

Key Takeaways:
• The Root of Addiction: Why all addictions, whether behavioral (food, sex, work) or chemical (drugs, alcohol), tap into the exact same reward centers in the brain.
• Connection Disorder: How addiction is ultimately a symptom of a profound lack of connection and an attempt to escape emotional pain.
• Developmental vs. Overt Trauma: The difference between horrific events happening to you and the absence of necessary emotional support during childhood.
• The Flawed Prison System: Why you "cannot punish pain out of people," and how punitive systems actively keep people entrenched in their addictions.
• Plant Medicines & Psychedelics: The rising potential of substances like MDMA, Psilocybin, and Ibogaine to shift consciousness and treat deep psychological wounds.
• Vulnerability as Strength: Why owning your vulnerability never compromises your credibility, and how hiding it only deepens trauma.
• Forgiveness vs. Letting Go: Why forced forgiveness (especially with narcissists) can be damaging, and how to find peace simply by putting the burden down.
• Boundaries for Givers: How to identify "yellow flags" in business and life to stop takers from exploiting your empathy.

snippet.title: How to Have a Stress-Free Political Conversation ft. James Carroll
snippet.description:
Joe's Free Book: https://joesfreebook.com/

If you’d like to join world-renowned Entrepreneurs at the next Genius Network® Event – then apply today for your invitation to attend at https://geniusnetwork.com/event/.

We've all been told to avoid talking about politics, but what if those conversations could actually deepen our understanding of the world and strengthen our relationships?

In this talk, James Carroll, National Chairman of the Benjamin Franklin Party, reveals why political discussions are often so stressful—and how to fix them. He starts by "breaking the frame," reminding us that 95% of political debates won't change the fate of Western civilization. Once the pressure is off, he introduces his simple, 4-step communication framework: The RASCAL Wheel.

Key Takeaways:
- The Reframe: Why the goal of a political conversation should never be to "win" a debate, but to deepen understanding and strengthen relationships.
- The Low Stakes Reality: Why letting go of the idea that you have to "save the world" in every conversation removes the stress.
- The RASCAL Wheel Framework: 
Respect: Why bidirectional respect must be the hub of every conversation.
     • Ask: How to ask open-ended, open-minded questions to uncover your own blind spots.
     • Sense: Moving beyond active listening to read body language and emotional states.
     • Check: How to paraphrase and ensure you actually understand the other person's point.
     • ALign: How to find common ground on values or goals, even if you disagree on the methods.
- The "I Statement" Rule: How to share your own views using irrefutable personal experiences.
- How to Exit Gracefully: What to say when a conversation starts going off the rails.

What happens when you combine the nomadic freedom of "Van Life" with the rugged sustainability of "Overlanding"? You get a movement.

In this interview, Joe Polish sits down with Jeffrey Hunter, Founder and CEO of Storyteller Overland, to discuss how he built a $200 million company from scratch in just four years. Jeffrey shares the origin story of Storyteller Overland, why they transitioned away from building "private jets on wheels," and how they engineered a vehicle designed to help people become the heroes of their own stories.

Joe also shares his personal journey of discovering the van life community, why he plans to use a Sprinter van as a mobile podcast studio and ADD-friendly workspace, and how you can use the "Write Yourself a Swimming Pool" concept to manifest the tools and experiences you want in your own life.

• The story behind Storyteller Overland and why Jeffrey started his adventure van company
• What the van life is all about (PLUS: How Jeffrey engages with his adventure-loving customers)
• How to create an even more E.L.F. (Easy, Lucrative & Fun) life with an Overland Storyteller
• The role of storytelling in the world of Overlanding and inspiring stories Jeffrey has heard

• How to integrate running a business and having outdoor adventures (Advice for striking a balance)

Joe Polish sits down with actor and comedian Rob Schneider to discuss his willingness to risk his career and face public backlash in defense of his beliefs. Rob shares his thoughts on the current political climate, the consequences of "cancel culture," and his new venture in a ghost town gold and silver mine. The conversation explores the shifting values of younger generations, the importance of free speech in comedy, and why Rob advocates for a return to traditional American values.

Key Takeaways
• A New Venture: Why Rob Schneider got involved in a gold and silver mine venture located in a western ghost town.
• Free Speech Statistics: According to a FIRE media organization survey, 36% of young people now feel it is acceptable to use violence to silence speech they disapprove of, compared to 99.9% who opposed such violence a decade ago.
• Campus Shifts: How Charlie Kirk helped drive a 22.5% bump in university-level young people identifying as conservative.
• Canadian Economics: The startling statistics that 40% of the highest earners have left Canada, while 40% of all workers in the country are now employed by the government.
• Hollywood's Peak Monopoly: The history of Hollywood's global dominance in the 1990s, when the industry controlled 92% of the world's films, prompting an 11% tax from France during the Clinton administration.
• Cultural Threats: Why Rob believes the "Red and Green Alliance" and woke culture represent a "superficial revolution" that threatens the fabric of the country.
• COVID-19 Fallout: Rob's assertion that 10,000 businesses and 10,000 restaurants went bankrupt during COVID lockdowns.
• The Devaluation of the Dollar: The economic reality of quantitative easing, with Rob noting a 52% devaluation of the dollar's buying power since 2009 according to the Department of Labor and Statistics.
• Handling Hate: How Rob handles death threats and personal confrontations, including an incident where he chose to respond with love during an angry confrontation with Robert De Niro at Saturday Night Live.

What if 60% of the bridges built this year collapsed? What if 60% of plane flights failed? We wouldn't tolerate it—yet a 60% to 70% failure rate is the accepted norm in the addiction recovery industry.

Jimmy Applegate, founder of Beacon Treatment Centers, exposes the structural flaws of a broken system. The standard treatment model relies on a 30-day program funded by insurance, but neuroscience proves it takes 6 to 18 months of immersive work to truly rewire an addicted brain.

Jimmy shares raw, real-world stories of recovery, breaks down the financial conflict of interest behind high relapse rates, and provides a clear, compassionate roadmap for families trying to pull a loved one out of active addiction.

Key Takeaways:
• The Repeat Customer Revenue Loop: How a 60% relapse rate funnels clients back through the front door, generating hundreds of thousands of dollars in additional revenue based on treatment failure.
• The Failure of One-Size-Fits-All: Why treating addiction with a cookie-cutter approach fails when recovery must be highly customized and individualized.
• The 4 Doors of Transformation: A deep dive into the psychological path an addict takes from the initial "Event" to absolute "Surrender," discovering "Hope," and finally achieving total "Transformation".
• The S.O.S. Framework: A simple, non-judgmental blueprint to guide your first conversation with an addict so they actually accept help and stay sober.

We all set goals and push hard, but what happens after you finally win? For many high achievers, success can quietly become a stopping point instead of a launching pad. In this presentation, Michael Bernoff—founder of the Human Communications Institute—explains how top performers mentally position themselves to move past their biggest goals. By focusing not just on the initial win, but the "second biggest win," Michael shows you how to future pace your success so that decisions become clearer and performance becomes easier. Whether you are a UFC fighter, a competitive figure skater, or an entrepreneur trying to overcome a revenue ceiling, this framework will teach you how to win not once, but twice.

Key Takeaways
• The Problem with Winning: Why 99% of people, even high achievers in high-level rooms, fall short of their ultimate capabilities due to conflicting internal tendencies.
• Redefining Future Pacing: Discover the true definition of future pacing: the ability to presuppose success in advance and build a new neuropathway.
• The "Second Biggest Win": How asking clients or yourself, "Do you know the second biggest win you're going to get from this?" immediately presupposes the first win is already accomplished.
• Real-World Application: How this exact mental framework helped a UFC fighter achieve a top 10 takedown and helped Michael's daughter master a double axel on the ice.
• Overcoming Plateaus: Why focusing on the moment after the trophy or the sale prevents you from stopping short of your goals and keeps your momentum high.

snippet.title: The Psychological Trick To Make People Buy from You Feat. Benjamin Hardy and Robert Cialdini
snippet.description:
Joe's Free Book: https://joesfreebook.com/

If you’d like to join world-renowned Entrepreneurs at the next Genius Network® Event – then apply today for your invitation to attend at https://geniusnetwork.com/event/.

How do you make your prospects more receptive before you even make an offer? What separates ethical influence from manipulation? In this compilation of powerful insights from the Genius Network stage, top minds in marketing, psychology, and entrepreneurship break down the true mechanics of persuasion and leadership.

Featuring Robert Cialdini (author of Influence and Pre-Suasion), Dan Sullivan, Steven Pressfield, Benjamin Hardy, and Joe Polish, they explore how to align your customer's identity with their goals, why you must transition from being the "Hero" to the "Sage," and the ethical responsibilities of high-level marketing. You’ll also learn tactical strategies—like using a $7 "tripwire" to double webinar conversions and employing the "Iceberg Model" to move from transactional selling to timeless transformation.

Key Takeaways:
• Pre-Suasion (with Robert Cialdini): How priming your audience with specific words (like "adventurous") or images (like clouds vs. coins) alters what they value and how they buy.
• The $7 Commitment: Why charging a tiny fee for a pre-webinar onboarding process doubles show-up rates and sales conversions.
• The Sage vs. The Hero: Why positioning yourself as the "Hero" makes your client a victim, and why acting as the "Sage" (like Yoda) creates ultimate buyer safety.
• The Iceberg Model: How to elevate your sales pitch from shallow, transactional features to deep, timeless meaning.
• The Ethics of Entrepreneurship: Dan Sullivan, Steven Pressfield, and Joe Polish discuss the difference between true connection and con artistry, and why ethics is ultimately a function of your "time perspective."
• Showing Up in the Storm: A hilarious and moving lesson on why leaders must show up and execute, even when their personal day is completely falling apart.

snippet.title: Anyone Not Learning AI Is Taking A Huge Risk ft. Mark Rukavina
snippet.description:
Joe's Free Book: https://joesfreebook.com/

If you’d like to join world-renowned Entrepreneurs at the next Genius Network® Event – then apply today for your invitation to attend at https://geniusnetwork.com/event/.

How do you take a small idea in a spare bedroom and turn it into the industry leader in digitizing home movies and photos—running a nearly 100% automated 24/7 facility?

In this interview, Joe Polish speaks with Mark Rukavina, the founder of iMemories, about his 35-year journey of building, scaling, and selling three massive tech companies (most recently selling iMemories to Ancestry.com). Mark reveals the "behind-the-scenes" of his massive $20M R&D investment to create the "Netflix of home movies," how he secured a deal with Walgreens across 8,000 stores, and why his favorite word in the world is "Grit."

In This Video, You’ll Learn:
• The Vision of iMemories: How Mark automated a complex, cottage industry to digitize 8 billion legacy home movies in the U.S.
• Why Startups Fail with Corporate Hires: Why hiring executives from companies like Apple or HP can be a huge mistake for a scrappy startup.
• Building to Sell: Mark’s strategy for starting every business with the end in mind and ensuring it's valuable enough for a billion-dollar acquisition.
• The Power of AI in Business: How iMemories uses AI for automated scene-editing and upscaling 1980s VHS tapes to HD quality, saving half a million dollars a year in labor.
• Overcoming the "Founder's Trap": How to let go of perfectionism and avoid becoming the bottleneck in your own company's growth.
• The Hardest Part of Business: Why customer acquisition remains the toughest challenge—even after 35 years in business—and why marketing must always be a top priority.
• The Role of Grit: Why Mark credits grit (drive over many years) over raw intelligence for his success.
